diagnostic_evidence.quote: The Runge--Kutta method \cref{eq:RK} is called AS-stable if $I - z A$ is non-singular for all $z \in \C^-$ and $z b^T (I - z A)^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded for $z \in \C^-$.

issues.failure_explanation: To apply Nevanlinna, D(z) must satisfy ||D(z)||≤1. With the stated α, ||D(z)|| ≤ |z|, which is not bounded by 1 as |z|→∞. The correct normalization uses the AS-stable bound on z b^T(I-zA)^{-1}. Thus the proof as written does not establish the second uniform bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the normalization in the second Nevanlinna application with α^{-1} = sup_{z∈C^-} ||z b^T (I-zA)^{-1}||, which is finite by AS-stability.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma AS_ASI_stability_bounds is invalid as written, leaving the uniform bound on (b^T⊗Z)(I-A⊗Z)^{-1} unproven. Downstream results relying on this lemma are therefore not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Incorrect normalization in AS-stability bound proof
issues.why_classification: A local correction to a normalization constant; the lemma statement is true and the fix preserves all downstream claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \dy[1][i] &= \big(b^T \otimes Z\big) \big(I - A \otimes Z\big)^{-1} \left( \so{i} \otimes y^{(i)}(\ts) \right) \\ &\quad + \big(b^T \otimes I\big) \big(I - A \otimes Z\big)^{-1} \dg[0][i-1] +\qo{i} y^{(i)}(\ts) ,

issues.failure_explanation: The general recursion for Δy[1][i] includes the term (b^T⊗Z)(I-AZ)^{-1}(γ_i⊗y^{(i)}). For i=3, this term is (b^T⊗Z)(I-AZ)^{-1}(γ_3⊗y'''), but it is omitted from the displayed third-order expansion. Since γ_3 is not generally zero, the displayed equation is false.

failure_location.quote:
\dt^3 \, \qo{3} \, y^{(3)}(\ts) \\
        & \quad + \dt^3 \big(b^T \otimes I\big) \big(I - A \otimes Z\big)^{-1} \big(I \otimes g'(y_0)\big)\big(I - A \otimes Z\big)^{-1} \big( \so{2} \otimes y''(\ts) \big) \\
        & \quad + \order{\dt^4}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing term (b^T⊗Z)(I-AZ)^{-1}(γ_3⊗y''') in the h^3 part of eq:LTE_order_3.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative third-order LTE formula is incorrect. The general recursion in Lemma thm:LTE remains correct, so the main theoretical results are not affected.
issues.title: Missing term in third-order LTE expansion
issues.why_classification: A single missing term in an illustrative equation; the general recursion is correct, so a local correction suffices.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The term $\ac[i+1]$ in \cref{eq:sum2} then adds the missing lone tree to the sum (since $\comcoef([\treeroot^{i+1}]) = 1$)

issues.failure_explanation: The recursion defines v_{i+1} with linear term α[i], but the proof uses α[i+1]. For i=1, this would give v_2 = α[2] + ... instead of α[1] + ..., contradicting the recursion. The missing tree in T_{i+1} is [root^i] with φ=α[i], not [root^{i+1}]. Thus the proof's indexing is inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Shift the indices: replace α[i+1] by α[i] and [root^{i+1}] by [root^i] in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma abstractrec is invalid as written, so the tree representation theorem thm:LTE_trees is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Off-by-one index error in proof of abstract recursion lemma
issues.why_classification: A local off-by-one index correction in the proof; the lemma statement is correct and the repair is routine.

issues.failure_explanation: The tree [[[[][]]]] is obtained by adding a root above [[[][]]] (row 4c). Its order condition should be b^T A^{j} β with β∈V_{[[[][]]]}. Since V_{[[[][]]]} = span{A^{i+1}(c^3/6 - A c^2/2)}, the condition is b^T A^{i1+i2+i3+1}(c^3/6 - A c^2/2)=0. The table instead repeats the row 5g condition involving γ_2 and C. Thus row 5h is incorrect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the row 5h condition with $0 = b^T A^{i_1+i_2+i_3+1} (c^3/6 - A c^2/2)$.
issues.overall_effect: The list of semilinear order conditions up to order five contains an incorrect condition for tree 5h. The constructed methods only use conditions up to order four, so their validity is not affected.
issues.title: Incorrect semilinear order condition for tree 5h
issues.why_classification: A single incorrect row in a table of order conditions; not used for the constructed methods, so a local correction suffices.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mu(J) \coloneqq \max_{0 \neq x \in \R^{\nvar}} \frac{\langle x, J x \rangle}{\langle x, x \rangle} \leq 0.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem allows J with μ(J)≤0, including J=0 or singular J. For such J, Z=hJ has a zero eigenvalue. Since B(1) holds (semilinear order ≥1), R(0)=1, so R(Z) has eigenvalue 1 and I-R(Z) is singular. The definition of ξ_{n-1} uses (I-R(Z))^{-1}, which is undefined. Eq:Rcondition does not exclude z=0; it only excludes zeros of (1-R(z))/z, which is non-zero at z=0. The proof does not handle this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inverse in the definition of ξ_{n-1} with the analytic function F(τ;Z,t) = (I-R(Z))^{-1} ψ(τ;Z,t), which is well-defined by cancellation of the removable pole at z=0, or handle Z with zero eigenvalues by a limiting argument.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the superconvergence case q=p_SL+1 in Theorem convergence is incomplete for problems with zero eigenvalues in J. The theorem's claim may still hold, but the given proof is invalid for that case.
issues.title: Singular inverse in superconvergence proof for zero eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: A local technical gap in the proof for a degenerate case; the source already establishes the removable pole, so the repair is short and preserves the result.
